predictor.def: A variable used as an input to predict the response, written \(X_1,\dots,X_p\). Also called independent variable or feature.

response.def: The variable we want to predict or explain, written \(Y\). Also called dependent variable or target.

systematic.def: The part of \(Y\) explained by the inputs through the fixed, unknown function \(f\) in \(Y=f(X)+\varepsilon\).

error-term.def: The random part of \(Y\) the inputs cannot explain; mean zero and independent of \(X\).

prediction.def: Using \(\hat Y=\hat f(X)\) to guess \(Y\) for new inputs; \(\hat f\) may be a black box.

inference.def: Understanding how \(Y\) is related to each predictor (which matter, in which direction, how strongly); needs an interpretable \(\hat f\).

reducible-error.def: \([f(X)-\hat f(X)]^2\): the error caused by \(\hat f\) differing from \(f\); better methods or more data can shrink it.

irreducible-error.def: \(\Var(\varepsilon)\): the error no estimate of \(f\) can remove, because \(\varepsilon\) cannot be predicted from \(X\).

training-data.def: The observed pairs \((x_1,y_1),\dots,(x_n,y_n)\) used to fit (train) a method.

parametric.def: Assume a form for \(f\) with a fixed number of parameters (e.g. linear), then fit those parameters to the data.

non-parametric.def: Estimates \(f\) without assuming a fixed form, staying close to the data while remaining smooth; needs many observations.

least-squares.def: Fitting a model by choosing parameters that minimise the sum of squared differences between observed and fitted responses.

flexible.def: A model that can produce a wide range of shapes for \(\hat f\); usually more parameters and less interpretable.

overfitting.def: Following the noise in the training data too closely: low training error, but worse accuracy on new data than a less flexible model would give.

supervised.def: Learning from data where every observation \(x_i\) comes with a response \(y_i\).

unsupervised.def: Learning structure from observations \(x_i\) that have no response, e.g. clustering.

clustering.def: Unsupervised method that groups observations into relatively distinct clusters based on their measurements.

semi-supervised.def: Only \(m\lt n\) observations have a response; methods use both labelled and unlabelled observations.

quantitative.def: A variable taking numerical values on which arithmetic makes sense (age, income, price).

qualitative.def: A variable taking one of \(K\) classes or categories (yes/no, brand A/B/C).

regression.def: A supervised problem with a quantitative response.

classification.def: A supervised problem with a qualitative response.
